title: Local stage representatives for filtered colimits of module-valued sheaves
statement: Let C be a category with Grothendieck topology J, Λ a commutative ring, I a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and G : I → Sh(C, Mod_Λ) a diagram of module-valued sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let c be a colimit cocone of G. For every object U and section t of c.pt at U, there exists a covering sieve S on U such that for every f : V → U in S there exist i ∈ I and s ∈ G_i(V) with c_i(s) = t restricted along f. No finite-cover hypothesis, compatibility of the sections, or uniform choice of i is asserted. The object, morphism, coefficient and diagram universes are independent; the section-module universe is max of the coefficient and diagram universes.

source.place: Tag 0738, proof of (4), first local-representatives assertion; local-image subsheaf construction written by Y2 as a universe-independent proof.

proof.text: Define the subfunctor R of the underlying type presheaf of H = c.pt by sectionwise membership in the image of some coprojection. Cocone naturality proves restriction stability. IsFiltered.nonempty gives the zero section; IsFiltered.max and the cocone equations place sums in a common stage; linearity gives scalar stability. Thus each R(U) is a submodule.

Take Subfunctor.sheafify J R, the local-membership closure inside H. GrothendieckTopology.intersection_covering proves additive closure by intersecting the sieves witnessing membership of two sections. Scalar closure follows from superset_covering and linearity. These submodules form a module-valued presheaf K. Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify_isSheaf says the underlying type presheaf is a sheaf. To use independent universes, represent the module forgetful functor by the lifted rank-one module ULift Λ using evaluation at 1, so it preserves limits of arbitrary site size; it reflects such limits by factorization through AddCommGrpCat. Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp therefore proves K is a module-valued sheaf.

The coprojections of c factor through K, since R ≤ Subfunctor.sheafify J R. They form a cocone d. Its coprojections followed by the inclusion m : K → H equal those of c. IsColimit.hom_ext and IsColimit.fac show hc.desc d ≫ m = identity H. Apply this identity to t: t lies in the local-membership closure of R. By the definition of Subfunctor.sheafify, R.sieveOfSection t is covering, and its membership supplies precisely the required stage and section.

from.place: Local stage representatives in the finite local lift argument, before selection of a finite covering and synchronization of stages.

lean.statement: theorem filtered_module_sheaf_colimit_local_representatives {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (Λ : Type r) [CommRing Λ] (I : Type w) [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (G : I ⥤ Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max r w} Λ)) (c : Cocone G) (hc : IsColimit c) (U : C) (t : c.pt.obj.obj (op U)) : ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧ ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f → ∃ (i : I) (s : (G.obj i).obj.obj (op V)), ((c.ι.app i).hom.app (op V)).hom s = (c.pt.obj.map f.op).hom t
